docs.title: MIPI CSI LP (MIPI Camera Serial Interface LP Mode)
docs.text:
MIPI CSI (Mobile Industry Processor Interface Camera Serial Interface) is a standardized data transfer protocol specifically designed to connect image sensors (such as camera modules) to processors (such as mobile phones, tablets or embedded devices). It was developed by the MIPI Alliance to provide an efficient, low-power and high-speed data transfer channel.

docs.title: MIPI I3C 1.2
docs.text:
MIPI I3C is an extension of the I2C interface, so it still maintains the two-wire SCL (clock) and SDA (data) as I2C. The frequency of MIPI I3C SCL clock is defined in the spec up to 12.9 MHz, and generally it is 12.5 MHz. It supports three operating voltages: 1.2 V/1.8 V/3.3 V.

MIPI I3C is a new generation sensor interface specification that integrates multiple sensor interfaces in a unified specification, mainly to simplify sensor integration in smart phones, IoT devices, and automotive systems.

docs.title: MIPI SoundWire 1.2
docs.text:
SoundWire is a hardware interface and transport protocol developed by MIPI. It provides an expandable, simple, low-power, low-latency, two-wire (clock and data) bus for carrying multiple audio streams (for example between amplifiers and microphones) along with embedded control commands.

Max Clock Rate: 12.288 MHz

docs.text:

  • Data: Transfer data of SoundWire. Default is checked.

  • Delay: Fix the position of latching data. Default is 40.

  • Bank: There are two types of parameters setting files, Bank0 and Bank1. The Data port (DP) is the source or sink of the Payload Stream on the SoundWire bus, and the DP also divides the Payload Stream into one or more channels for each audio channel. Default is cleared.
  • Initial Frame Shape: set the row and column of each setting file. Default is cleared.

  • Show Packet Table: Show Packet Table (in 2-Dimension). Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is cleared.

  • Hide all Ping OPCode: Hide all the Ping OPCode in report. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is cleared.
  • Ignore SCP Frame Ctrl CMD: Hide all SCP CMD in report for easy reading. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is cleared.

Data Port (DPn) settings
  • DPn amount: 1~16, No. DP0~DP15. Default index is 0.
    • HStart: The start position of data in Frame Shape. Default is checked.
    • HStop: The stop position of data in Frame Shape. Default is cleared.
    • Word Length: Data length of each channel in DPn. Default is 0.
    • Sample Interval: DPn sample interval. Default is 98.
    • Block Package Mode:
      • Block per port: Block Offset = Offset1 + (256 * Offset2)
      • Block per channel: Block Offset = Offset1, Sub-Block Offset = Offset2.
      • *Block Offset range : 0 ~ 65535. Default is checked.
      • *Sub-Block Offset range: 0 to 255. Default is cleared.
      • *Offset1 range: 0~65535
      • *Offset2 range: 0~255
    • Channel: Divide a Data Port into separate parts, commonly used for left channel, right channel, and so on. You can use up to 8 channels, in any order.
    • Port Flow Mode: It has four modes: Isochronous, Tx-Controlled, Rx-Controlled, and Full-Asynchronous.
      • *Isochronous: ‘Normal’ mode, there is no valid data in each Payload Data Block. Default is cleared.
      • *Tx-Controlled: ‘Push’ mode, whether the flow-control bit driven by the Source Data Port transmits valid data in the Payload Data Block. Default is cleared.
      • *Rx-Controlled: ‘Pull’ mode, whether the flow-control bit driven by the Sink Data Port transmits valid data in the Payload Data Block. Default is cleared.
      • *Full-Asynchronous: Whether the flow-control bit driven by the Sink and Source Data Port transmits valid data in the Payload Data Block. Default is cleared.

docs.title: MMC/eMMC 4.5 (Embedded Multi Media Card)
docs.text:
The Multi Media Card (MMC) or the Embedded Multi Media Card (eMMC) version 5.1 is a flash memory card standard.

Wrong Bus Mode/width/latch settings cause decode failure; Command and Data can be analyzed separately. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
MMC/eMMC Decode Settings

  • Analysis:
    • Command: Analyze Command. Default is this mode selected.
    • Data: Analyze Data. Default is not selected.
  • Bus Mode: Legacy/High Speed/HS200/HS400. Default is High Speed.
  • Decode Startup Mode:
    • Bus Width: 1-bit/4-bit/8-bit Data. Default is 4-bit Data.
    • Latch Method: SDR/DDR. Default is DDR.
  • Boot Settings:
    • Bus Width: 1-bit/4-bit/8-bit Data. Default is 1-bit Data.
    • Latch Method: SDR/DDR. Default is SDR.
  • Options:
    • Adv. Report: Further decode results in the report. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • 3 Pin Mode: Analyze with CLK, CMD, and D0. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked (often field disabled (Disable)).
    • No CLK Mode: Analyze without CLK. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Auto Phase Correction: Automatic phase correction. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is checked.
    • Detect BOT ACK: Detect BOOT ACK when the DUT is not powered on. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • DS: Use Data Strobe. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked (often field disabled (Disable)).

docs.title: Modbus
docs.text:
Modbus is a serial communications protocol published by Modicon in 1979 for PLCs; it is now a common industrial interconnect.

Wrong Baud Rate, ASCII/RTU mode, or polarity fails decode—prefer Auto Detect. See Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
Modbus Decode Settings
  • Channel:
    • Tx: Modbus Tx channel.
    • Rx: Modbus Rx channel. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
  • Transmission Mode: ASCII / RTU. Default: RTU.
  • Format:
    • Auto Detect: Auto-detect manual options. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: checked.
    • Manual: Set the options below. Default: cleared.
      • Baud Rate: bits/s (about 110–2 M). Default: 9600.
      • Polarity: Idle high / Idle low. Default: Idle high.
      • Parity: None / Odd / Even. Default: None.
      • Data Bits: 7 / 8 / 9. Default: 8.
  • CRC Check: CRC check. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: checked.
  • Adv. Report: Further decode in the report. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
  • Big-Endian: Arrange data Big-Endian. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
  • Waveform Area Settings:
    • Decode: Show Tx or Rx in the waveform; Rx only when Rx is field enabled (Enable). Default conversion index often 0.
    • Show Scale: Show scale on the waveform. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: checked.

docs.title: NAND Flash SCA (NAND Flash Separate Command Address)
docs.text:
NAND Flash SCA (Separate Command Address) decodes NAND Flash traffic when Command/Address use a dedicated CA bus, unlike classic CLE/ALE sharing the data bus in NAND Flash. The plugin family is shared, but channel labels, Analysis Mode, and SCA Header are SCA-specific.

Wrong Analysis Mode, CA/CLK wiring, or Channel Phase Delay mis-decodes commands, addresses, or data. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
NAND Flash SCA Decode Settings
  • Device Width: Data width x8/x16. Default is x8.
  • I/O Quick Setup/I/O User Defined: Quick Setup only needs I/O0 (LSB); other I/O channels auto-expand. User Defined opens a dialog for each I/O channel. Default is I/O Quick Setup.
  • Channel: Assign SCA signals to logic analyzer channels (channel numbers omitted from Defaults).
    • I/O0 (LSB)/I/O range: Data lines; x16 adds upper I/O.
    • CA_CE: Chip Enable group. Use … to open CA_CE Groups (below) for multiple CE channels.
    • CA[1]/CA[0]: Command/Address bus bits.
    • CLK: CA clock.
    • DQS/DQS2: Data strobes. Checking DQS2 enables (Enable) the DQS2 channel; Default is unchecked.
    • RE/R/B: Read Enable and Ready/Busy.
  • Analysis Mode: SCA Only (CA/SCA packets only), DQ Only (data path only), or SCA (SCA plus data). Default is SCA.
  • SCA Header: Opens SCA Decode Reference (below) to map Header 0x0–0xF to Kind and decode method. Hidden/disabled when Analysis Mode is DQ Only.
  • Channel Phase Delay: CA sample-phase sliders for CA[1]/CA[0]. Default: CA[1] = 1, CA[0] = 5 (shown in ns when sample rate is known).
  • Data Out Cycles (tREA/tDQSQ): Read-data delay. Default is 5 for both (shown in ns when sample rate is known). Adjust if sampling on transitions yields bad values.
  • Options:
    • Hide Items: Show/hide report items by condition; use … after checking. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Show Erase Count: Show Erase command/address statistics. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Auto-fill Address Commands: Auto-fill report Address fields. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • SCA Advanced Report: More detailed SCA report output. Shown only when Analysis Mode is SCA; field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Device information:
    • Vendors: Select a matching or command-compatible vendor; Custom builds a command table (see NAND Flash). Default vendor is ONFI.
    • Model: Supported spec/model list. Default list index is 3 (commonly ONFI 4.0 for ONFI).
  • Bytes per report row: 8/16/24/32. Default is 16.

docs.title: CA_CE Groups
docs.text: Open with … next to CA_CE. Assign Channel and Used for CE0–CE7. Group 1 (primary CA_CE) is always enabled; other groups are enabled (Enable) when Used is checked. Default: only Group 1 enabled; other group channels are 0.

docs.title: SCA Header (SCA Decode Reference)
docs.text:
Opens from SCA Header. Maps Header 0x0–0xF to Kind (CA Packet Type) and decode method (Output/Input/VSP/Reserved). Saved as sca_decode_reference.txt in the work directory; Restore Default reloads the built-in table (e.g. 0x0 = CA Data Output/Output, 0x2 = Command/Input, 0x8 = CA Data Input/Input).

Shared Custom command tables (AqNFCustom.txt) and Timing Check format are described under NAND Flash.

docs.text:

docs.title: NAND Flash
docs.text:
Flash memory includes NOR and NAND types. NAND Flash offers higher density and lower cost per bit than NOR, but its I/O interface has no random-access external address bus and must be read in blocks. NAND Flash is common in USB drives and most memory cards.

Wrong Device Width, startup mode, or tREA/tDQSQ settings misread data. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
NAND Flash Decode Settings
  • Channel: Assign CLE, ALE, RE, WE, CE, R/B, DQS, and I/O channels.
  • Device Width: Select 8/16-bit data width. Default is x8.
  • I/O Quick Setup/I/O User Defined: Quick Setup only needs I/O0 (LSB); other I/O channels auto-expand. User Defined opens a dialog to set each I/O channel. Default is I/O Quick Setup.
I/O User Defined
  • Flash Startup/Analysis Mode: Includes SDR and Toggle/ONFI DDR. Default is Toggle/ONFI DDR (index 1).
  • tREA/tDQSQ (and tDS/tDH): Delay for reading NAND data in SDR/DDR. Devices often provide presets; adjust if sampling on transitions yields bad data. Default slider values are commonly 5.
  • Save the NAND Flash Data: Save Read/Write data as Bin under the LA work directory. Field enabled (Enable) when checked.
  • Don't show BUSY state: Show/hide BUSY START/BUSY END in the report. Field enabled (Enable) when checked.
  • Show Erase Count: Show Erase command/address statistics. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Hide Items: Show/hide report items by condition. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Invert RE# (W/R#)/Invert DQS: Use when RE/DQS# are inverted in DDR mode. Field enabled (Enable) when checked.
  • Not filled address/Auto-fill Address: When auto-fill is off, addresses are computed and filled; when on, address fields are not filled. Default: Auto-fill Address unchecked.
  • Don't care ALE/CE#/RB#: Ignore selected pins; ignoring ALE requires 2 or 3 byte Row Address. Field enabled (Enable) when checked.
  • Bytes per report row: 8/16/24/32. Default is 16.
  • Saved file name example: e.g. NF_DI_Row017821h_Col0000h_CE1_1.bin; compare with the report.
  • Device information:
    • Vendors: Select a matching or command-compatible device; Custom builds a command table (below). Default vendor is ONFI.
    • Model: Supported NAND Flash model. Default model list index is 3.
  • Custom command table: Create AqNFCustom.txt in the LA work directory when Vendor is Custom. Keywords Manufacturer, PartNo, #CE/RB, X16, SyncMode, and Cmd are required and must not be changed.
  • Example lines: Cmd=Read, Read, tR, 60, , , N, N, N, 00, 30; Cmd=Read Status, Read Stat., , , , , Y, N, Y ,70; Cmd=Two-Plane Page Program, TPP Prog., tDBSY, 1, tPROG, 5000, N, Y, N, 80, 11, 81, 10.
  • Field notes:
    • Full/abbreviated names: e.g. Read Status/Two-Plane Page Program vs Read Stat./TPP Prog. for short waveform labels.
    • Busy Time Check: e.g. tDBSY = 1 µs, tPROG = 5000 µs; violations appear in the report. Leave blank with commas to skip; names are user-defined.
    • Three flags: For Cmd=Read Status, Read Stat., Y, N, Y ,70: 1st Y = allowed during Busy; 2nd N = insertion restricted; 3rd Y = may insert into multi-step commands (e.g. 70h between 11h and 81h of Two-Plane Page Program). Custom shows the file vendor/model and decodes by the command list.
  • Timing Check: Add the following at the top of AqNFCustom.txt when needed.
    • Spec: ONFI or Toggle only.
    • Version: ONFI: SDR/NV-DDR/NV-DDR2-3; Toggle: Legacy/1.0/2.0.
    • TimingCheck: Y/N. Format: Item Name, Min, Max (ns). Use appendix item names for the selected Spec/Version; others are ignored. Use X to skip a bound; both X skips the item.
    • Results: Information field: red = out of range, black = OK; includes item, measured time, and limits.
    • Average notes: tDQSH/tDQSL: 0.45 × tDSC(avg); tQSH/tQSL: 0.37 × tRC(avg); tREH/tRP: 0.43 × tRC(avg). Add the matching header lines when using averages; otherwise UsedtRCavg=N/UsedtDSCavg=N or Min/Max values.

docs.title: NEC IR (NEC Infrared Transmission Protocol)
docs.text:
NEC IR (NEC Infrared Transmission Protocol) is a common infrared remote-control encoding protocol used between remotes and receivers.

Wrong Extended/bit-order settings misread Address/Command fields. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
NEC IR Decode Settings
  • Channel: Set the LA channel for the NEC signal.
  • Options:
    • Extended Mode: Merges /Address and Address into a 16-bit Address, and /Command and Command into a 16-bit Command. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Display without idle in report: Hides Idle rows in the report. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Swap Bits: Switch from LSB First to MSB First. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Ignore glitch: Ignore glitches during analysis. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.

docs.title: OA3p(PMD) (Open Alliance 3-pin)
docs.text:
OA3p (OPEN Alliance 3-pin) is an important protocol in automotive Ethernet testing that defines PHY test requirements for consistency, reliability, and stability under different operating conditions.

Wrong display mode or Ethernet/MDIO options omit or misread report fields. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
OA3p(PMD) Decode Settings
  • Channel: Set OA3p channels (TX/RX_MDC/ED_MDO).
  • OA3p settings:
    • Display Mode: Show TX Data + Config or RX Data + Config in the waveform. Default is TX Data + Config.
    • Show Rx Data in NORMAL State: Keep showing RX results in Normal State. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Ethernet Settings (10BaseT1S): Configure Ethernet parsing in the report. Related options are field enabled (Enable) when the group is checked.
    • Show Sync Code: Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Show 5B Code: Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Show MAC Data: Optionally show Transport Layer Data or Transport Layer Data & Header. Default is checked (type commonly Transport Layer Data).
    • Show Single BEACON: Related to Hide Beacon; Default is Hide Beacon unchecked.
    • FCS in Byte Order: Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Data Filter: Show only the set number of bytes. Field enabled (Enable) for length when checked. Default is unchecked; length commonly 20 bytes.
    • Report Data: Bytes per data field row (8/16/32 Byte). Default is 8 Byte.
  • MDIO Settings (Config State):
    • Enable Preamble Counter: Set preamble bit count. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked; count commonly 32.
    • Data Edge: Latch on rising or falling edge. Default is Rising.

docs.title: OATC6 over SPI (Open Alliance SPI)
docs.text:
OPEN Alliance Technical Committee 6 (TC6) focuses on improving the media-independent communication interface (xMII) for automotive networks and defines related recommendations.

Wrong Protected Mode, Timestamp, or Block Payload settings misdecode control/data frames. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
OATC6 over SPI Decode Settings
  • Channel: Set OATC6 channels (CLK/CS/SDI/SDO).
  • Report Settings:
    • Show Ctrl Detail: Show Ctrl detail in the report. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is checked.
    • Waveform Display: Show SDI or SDO decode in the waveform. Default is SDI.
  • Startup Settings:
    • Protected Mode: Enable or disable protected format in the control frame. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Enable Timestamp: Field enabled (Enable) for 64-bit/32-bit timestamp format when checked. Default is unchecked; format commonly 64-bit (Default).
    • Block Payload Size: 64-Byte/32-Byte. Default is 64-Byte (Default).
    • Transmit FCS Validation Enable: Enable FCS validation on transmit. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Ethernet Settings:
    • FCS Byte Order: Present FCS in byte order. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Data Filter: Show only N bytes (minimum 20). Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked; length commonly 20 bytes.
    • Report Data: Max bytes per Data field row (8/16/32). Default is 8 Byte.
    • Show Ethernet Packet: Show Address, Data, FCS, and related fields. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.

docs.title: PCM
docs.text:
The format that describes sound as a series of numbers is often called a raw audio file; the term is PCM (Pulse-code modulation). Examples include WAV on Windows and AIFF on Apple platforms, typically with a header at the beginning.

Wrong Data bits, mode, Latch Edge, or Enable Pulse settings cause decode failure. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
PCM Decode Settings
  • Channel: Set PCM channels (SCK/CS/SD).
  • Audio Settings:
    • Data bits: PCM data bit width (8/16/24/32). Default is 16.
    • Mode: PCM A Mode/PCM B Mode/PCM Multi Mode. Default is PCM A Mode.
    • Channel Count: Number of channels (1–8 or Unlimit). Default is 2.
    • Latch Edge: Latch on Falling/Rising clock edge. Default is Falling.
    • Enable Pulse: CS active level High/Low. Default is High.
    • Enable full scale: Full-scale function. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • LSB First: Arrange data LSB first. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Sound Reduction: Display, play, or save the audio waveform. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: display/playback/save are all unchecked; playback length is commonly All.

docs.title: PDM (Pulse-Density Modulation)
docs.text:
PDM (Pulse Density Modulation) is a digital modulation technique mainly used for digitizing and transmitting audio.

Wrong mono/stereo, sample rate, or Decimation settings distort restored audio. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
PDM Decode Settings
  • Channel: Set Clk and Data channels.
  • Detail:
    • Mono & Stereo: Mono or stereo capture mode. Default is Mono (latch commonly Rising; Stereo latch often field disabled (Disable)).
    • PDM Sample Rate: PDM clock rate; Auto Detect available. Default: Auto Detect checked; manual value commonly 4800.
    • Decimation Parameter: Decimation ratio (x16–x2048), mutually exclusive with Audio Frequency. Default selects Decimation, commonly x64.
    • Audio Frequency: PCM audio frequency (kHz). Field enabled (Enable) when selected. Default is not selected (value commonly 192 kHz).
  • Sound reduction:
    • Playback: Field enabled (Enable) when checked; duration 3 Sec/5 Sec/All. Default: playback checked, duration 3 Sec.
    • Display audio waveform: Field enabled (Enable) when checked; draw Full Scale or Original. Default: display unchecked; draw Original.
    • Save as WAV file: Save restored audio as .wav. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.

docs.title: PMBus (Power Management Bus)
docs.text:
PMBus (Power Management Bus) is an open power-management communications standard published in 2005 (Artesyn and partners) for data transfer, commands, and formats (similar in spirit to smart-battery standards).

Wrong address mode or PEC options yields wrong reports. See Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
PMBus Decode Settings
  • Channel:
    • Clock Channel (SCK): PMBus clock.
    • Data Channel (SDA): PMBus data.
  • Options:
    • 8-bit addressing (Including R/W in Address): Show 8-bit address (7-bit + Rd/Wr). Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
    • PEC decode: Include PEC in analysis. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
  • Clock Stretching: Configure clock stretching. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared (timeout blank).

docs.title: Profibus (Process Field Bus)
docs.text:
ProfiBus (PROcess Field Bus) was developed in 1987 by Siemens and other companies and research institutes in Germany, and is widely used in industrial control, transportation, and power automation. It consists of PROFIBUS FMS (Fieldbus Message Specification), PROFIBUS DP (Decentralized Peripherals), and PROFIBUS PA (Process Automation). PROFIBUS DP and PROFIBUS PA are the most commonly used today.

Wrong Baud Rate, Start bit, or bit order causes decode failure; prefer Auto Detect first. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
Profibus Decode Settings
  • Channel: Set the ProfiBus signal channel.
  • Baud Rate/Auto Detect: Set baud rate manually or enable Auto Detect. Field enabled (Enable) for Auto Detect when checked. Default is Auto Detect checked; baud text is commonly 9600.
  • Start bit: High/Low. Default is Low.
  • MSB first: Use MSB after the Start bit; unchecked uses LSB. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Show scale in the waveform: Show bit scale by baud rate in the waveform. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.

docs.title: PS/2 (Personal System/2)
docs.text:
PS/2 is a bidirectional synchronous serial protocol for communication between a keyboard or mouse and a PC. Developed by IBM, it uses six pins: Clock, Data, +5 V, Ground, and two unused pins. The two ends exchange data over Clock and Data.

Wrong device type, Scan Code, or mouse type misreads the report. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
PS/2 Decode Settings
  • Channel: Set Clock and Data channels.
  • Export MATLAB file: Export analyzed data as MATLAB format (Time/Description/Data; DH = Device to Host, HD = Host to Device). The file (PS2_Matlab.m) is saved in the work directory. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Device:
    • Keyboard: Treat the device as a PS/2 keyboard.
    • Mouse: Treat the device as a PS/2 mouse.
    • Other (Only Display Raw Data): Other PS/2 devices; show raw data only. Default is this mode selected.
  • Startup Setting:
    • Scan Code: Keyboard Scan Code Set (Set 1/2/3). Default is Set 2.
    • Mouse Type: Mouse type (Standard/Scroll Wheel/Five Button). Default is Standard PS/2 Mouse.

docs.title: PSI5 (Peripheral Sensor Interface 5)
docs.text:
PSI5 (Peripheral Sensor Interface 5) is an open automotive sensor interface used to connect peripheral sensors to electronic control units. It is widely applied in safety-related and sensor-intensive vehicle systems, and is designed for robust, cost-efficient digital communication over a small number of wires.

In the Logic Analyzer, the PSI5 decode plugin reconstructs the sensor frame structure from the captured waveform so you can inspect timing, payload fields, and check results without decoding the bus manually.

Wrong Bit Rate, Polarity, Manchester, or Version yields incorrect frames. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
PSI5 Decode Settings
  • Channel: Logic Analyzer channel for the PSI5 data signal (UI label may show Configuration Channel).
  • Color: Display colors for Start, Data, and CRC/Parity on the waveform.
  • Startup:
    • Bit Rate: 125 kbps / 189 kbps / Custom. Default: 125 kbps.
    • Custom (ns): Bit period in nanoseconds when Bit Rate is Custom. Field enabled (Enable) when Bit Rate is Custom. Default text when resetting: 8000.
    • # of Data Bits: Data bits per sensor frame. Default: 10.
    • Error Check: Even Parity / Odd Parity / CRC-3 / None. Default: Even Parity.
    • Tolerance: Allowed timing tolerance for bit detection. Default: 20%.
    • Polarity: Idle Low / Idle High. Default: Idle Low.
    • Manchester: Normal / Inverted. Default: Normal.

docs.title: J1850
docs.text:
SAE J1850 is an automotive communications protocol used mainly for on-board diagnostics (OBD) and in-vehicle networking. Before CAN became standard, it was widely used in vehicles. J1850 lets electronic control units (ECUs) communicate in the vehicle.

Wrong bit order, invert setting, or PWM/VPW timing yields incorrect frames. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
SAE J1850 Decode Settings
  • Channel: J1850 signal channel.
  • Bit order: MSB First/LSB First. Default: MSB First.
  • Invert waveform: Invert the waveform for analysis. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
  • Manufacture: Manufacturer (affects NB/CRC behavior). Field enabled (Enable) only when Transfer Method is VPW; field disabled (Disable) for PWM. Currently GM and Chrysler; contact us for more options. Default is not reset by the Default button.
  • Transfer Method: PWM or VPW (different timing groups; editable). PWM enables (Enable) the PWM timing group and disables (Disable) VPW timing plus Manufacture/NB color; VPW does the opposite. Default: VPW.
  • PWM timing (µs): Field enabled (Enable) when Transfer Method is PWM. Parameters and Defaults:
    • Active Phase "1": Active pulse width for logic 1. Default: 8 µs.
    • Active Phase "0": Active pulse width for logic 0. Default: 16 µs.
    • Bit Time: Full bit period. Default: 24 µs.
    • SOF/EOD Time: Start of Frame/End of Data duration. Default: 48 µs.
    • EOF Time: End of Frame duration. Default: 72 µs.
    • IFS Time: Inter-Frame Separation. Default: 96 µs.
    • Active SOF: Active pulse width of SOF. Default: 32 µs.
    • Active BRK: Active pulse width of Break. Default: 40 µs.
    • BRK to IFS Time: Time from Break end to IFS. Default: 120 µs.
  • VPW timing (µs): Field enabled (Enable) when Transfer Method is VPW. Default: Short Pulse 64, Long Pulse 128, SOF/EOD Time 200, EOF Time 280, BRK Time 300, IFS Time 300.

docs.title: SafeSPI (Serial Peripheral Interface for Automotive Safety)
docs.text: SafeSPI standardises the use of SPI for automotive sensor data. Plain SPI defines the electrical and clock relationship but nothing about the content — no address, no checksum, no status — so SafeSPI adds a logical layer on top of the same four wires: fixed 32-bit or 48-bit frames, a target address on the command and a source address on the response, a CRC on every frame, sensor status bits, and timing limits for the bus. This decode implements Rev 2.0, which is backward compatible with Rev 1.0 — the CRC definitions and test vectors are identical and 48-bit frames are the v2.0 addition, so no version selector is needed.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
Decode Settings
  • Data Line: Select which line the waveform strip shows, MOSI (Command) or MISO (Response). Both lines are always decoded whichever is selected — SafeSPI is full duplex and the two lines' field boundaries do not align, so one strip cannot hold both. To see both as two strips, add this decode a second time set to the other line. The report is not restricted this way; see Report both directions below. Default: MOSI (Command).
  • Frame Length: Select Auto, 32 Bit or 48 Bit. Auto counts the SCK cycles inside the chip-select window and cross-checks the CRC, which is the detection method the standard provides for this. The resolved width is shown in the report settings row as 32oof (Auto). Default: Auto.
  • Mode: Select Out-of-Frame (Mode 0), In-Frame (Mode 1) or Auto. Out-of-frame samples on the rising SCK edge and the slave's answer arrives in the next frame; in-frame samples on the falling edge and the answer is inside the same frame. Auto scores the CRC variants against both edge streams. Disabled when Frame Length is 48 Bit, which is out-of-frame only. Default: Auto.
  • Frame Format: Select FlexFrame or FixedSensorFrame. This cannot be auto-detected: the two use the same bits and produce the same valid CRC, and differ only in whether those bits carry defined fields. FlexFrame leaves them free to use; FixedSensorFrame defines RW, CAP and DATAI on the command. Choosing Fixed for a Flex bus fabricates fields that do not exist, so the default is the safe one. Default: FlexFrame.
  • Slave Address: Select how the target and source addresses split into a slave address and a slave-internal address: SelSlaveByCS (one chip select per slave), Sel2SlaveByAdrPin, Sel2SlaveByAdrNVM, Sel4SlaveByAdrPin or Sel4SlaveByAdrNVM. Default: SelSlaveByCS.
  • CS active high: SafeSPI asserts chip select LOW. Check this if the capture was taken through an inverting probe or the device uses the opposite polarity. Default: unchecked.
  • SCK idle high (CPOL = 1): SafeSPI idles the clock LOW. Check this for a bus that idles high; the sampling edge is normalised accordingly. Default: unchecked.
  • Verify CRC: Check each frame's CRC. SafeSPI has four CRC variants — 32-bit out-of-frame, 32-bit in-frame command, 32-bit in-frame response and 48-bit — with different coverage ranges; the decoder selects the right one for each frame. The CRC cell is green when it matches and red when it does not. Default: checked.
  • All-zero MISO frame = no response: Treat a response frame whose bits are all zero as the slave not answering, and report it instead of decoding the zeros. This is a derived rule rather than a stated one — it relies on the Rev 2.0 requirement for a MISO pull-down, which Rev 1.0 does not have — so it is off until a real capture confirms it. When on, the Information column states the evidence as Assumed Hi-Z. Default: unchecked.
  • Decode FrTyp bit: Interpret the FrTyp bit as announcing the width of the next frame. This only applies to a device implementing the mixed 48/32-bit option with address-selected width; elsewhere the bit is free to use and announces nothing. The field itself is always shown — this setting only controls whether the interpretation is added to the Information column. Default: unchecked.
  • Report both directions: List the command and the response in one report, two rows per frame, with a Dir column saying which is which. The waveform strip still shows the Data Line only. Turn it off for a single-direction report matching the strip. Default: checked.
  • Check bus timing: Measure the bus against the timing tables of the standard — SCK high and low times, chip-select lead and lag, sequential transfer delay, and the setup, hold and valid times of both data lines. Violations are listed at the top of the report by requirement number with the measured worst value, the limit and where it happened. A limit the capture's sample rate cannot resolve is counted but never judged. Default: checked.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
With Report both directions on, the report shows two rows per frame. Dir says whether the row is the command or the response, and the shared columns then hold whichever field that direction defines: Addr is the target address on a MOSI row and the source address on a MISO row, Data is DATAI or DATAO, and Flags carries CAP and FrTyp on a command row or IDS, CE and DCnt on a response row. D and Status apply to responses only.

Pairs shows the request/response relationship, which is not visible from row order alone: out-of-frame answers arrive one frame late, so the two rows of a single frame are not a pair. On a command row the cell names the source address of the response that came back; on a response row it names the target address of the command being answered. A blank cell means the counterpart was not observed — at the end of the capture, or before the first command — and a red dash means the command was seen to go unanswered.

The first report row always states the SCK frequency measured from the capture itself, followed by the settings the decode ran with. The CRC cell is green when the checksum matches and red when it does not. Notes that are not faults, such as a sensor in its initialisation state, go to the Information column rather than to Error.

docs.title: SDR SDRAM
docs.text:
SDRAM (Synchronous Dynamic Random Access Memory) is a synchronous dynamic random access memory. Its characteristic is that it can synchronize the memory clock with the Host. Because it can only transmit data on the Rising edge, SDRAM can also be called SDR SDRAM (Single Data Rate SDRAM).

SDRAM differs from the DDR SDRAM structure used in current computers. DDR (Double Data Rate) actually refers to DDR SDRAM (Double Data Rate SDRAM), meaning Rising/Falling edges can both transmit data.

Due to the large number of channels required and the high signal speed, this decode is only available on LA3000+, LA4000+, or BusFinder models. In addition, this decode only supports SDR SDRAM analysis, not DDR SDRAM.

For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
SDR SDRAM Decode Settings
  • Channel: Assign the Logic Analyzer channels for SDRAM signals (#CAS, CKE, #CS, #RAS, #WE, A10, and Address/Data/DQM as needed).
  • Parsing include Address and Data: Field enabled (Enable) when checked for full analysis with all SDRAM pins. When unchecked, only a simple Command analysis is performed (connect #CAS, CKE, #CS, #RAS, #WE, and A10 — 6 channels), reducing wiring but without Address/Data status; suitable for basic analysis. Default is checked.
  • DQM / Address / Data width: Select DQM (x1/x2/x4), Address (x12/x13), and Data (x32/x16/x8/x4). Default is DQM x4, Address x12, Data x32.
  • Startup — #CAS Latency: Set the SDRAM read latency (Non / 2 clocks / 3 clocks). Default is Non.
  • Decode display in waveform area: SDRAM has many states that cannot all be shown at once; select Command / Address / Data / Bank Address / A10. To view multiple items at once, add multiple SDRAM decode groups with different display modes. Default is Command.

docs.title: SENT (Single Edge Nibble Transmission)
docs.text:
The SENT (Single Edge Nibble Transmission) protocol is used in automotive electronics for data transmission between sensors and ECUs (for example wheel-speed or position sensors). It supports efficient, high-precision transfer within limited bandwidth.

Incorrect Clock Tick, Tolerance, # of Nibbles, SENT Version, or Message format relative to the device causes decode failures. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.text:

    • Clock Tick: Tick time (µs). Default is 3 us.

    • # of Nibbles: Number of data nibbles (1–8). Default is 6.
    • Polarity: Idle Low / Idle High. Default is Idle High.
    • SENT Version: 2008 / 2010/2016. Default is 2010/2016. When 2008 is selected, Pause/CRC fields are disabled (Disable).
    • Pause: OFF / ON (SENT 2010/2016). Default is OFF.
    • Message: Fast Channel / Short Channel / Enhanced Serial. Default is Fast Channel.
    • CRC: Legacy / Recommended (SENT 2010/2016). Default is Recommended.

docs.title: Serial Flash (OSPI)
docs.text:
Serial flash (SPI Flash) 25, 35, and similar series use SPI/QPI/OPI as their data-transfer protocol. Serial flash bus analysis lets you view commands and input/output bus messages together, saving time versus analyzing waveforms with a generic SPI decode.

Incorrect Manufacturer/device, startup mode, or tCLQV/tSHSL settings cause command-parse failures. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
Serial Flash (OSPI) Decode Settings
  • CS#: Chip Select of the transfer signal.
  • SCLK: Clock of the transfer signal.
  • SIO0–SIO7: Data pins of the transfer signal.
  • Manufacturer: Select the correct Flash model, tCLQV, and tSHSL for command parsing. If no exact model exists, choose a command-compatible model. Default is the first manufacturer/device entry.
  • The Flash Startup Mode: Serial Flash can switch modes by command; when waveforms are captured, the analyzer does not know the current mode, so the user must set it when needed. Options unsupported by the selected model are disabled (Disable).
    • QPI Mode: Quad Peripheral Interface Mode (Quad SPI Mode). Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • 4-Byte Mode: 4-Byte Address Mode. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • PEM Mode: Performance Enhancement Mode. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Dummy Cycles: Preset Dummy-cycle count for some Read commands. Field enabled (Enable) when the related option is checked.
    • Wrap Around: Preset Wrap-around value. Field enabled (Enable) when the related option is checked.
    • QE bit: QE bit in the status register for QPI enable/disable. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
    • Startup in Octal Mode: OPI mode; STR/DTR become enabled (Enable) when Octal is checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Security Field: AES encrypt/decrypt Flash support; contact us if needed. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Decode SI Only: Analyze in Single mode with 3 wires (CS# / SCLK / SI). Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Decode Single Mode Only: Analyze in Single mode with 4 wires (CS / Clock / SI / SO) and ignore multi-line switch commands; when unchecked, analyze as 4-wire or 6-wire per Flash model. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • When Command Unknown: Decode SO or SI only. Default is SI only.
  • Always in PEM Mode: Stay in PEM regardless of commands; choose STR or DTR. Field enabled (Enable) when checked (enables STR/DTR). Default is unchecked.
  • Reduce Read Status (05h): Merge repeated Read Status (05h) with unchanged data and show the repeat count. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Read Status: Parse Read Status. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is checked.
  • Read data on the rising edge of CLK: For SDR Read Data, if Clock duty is unstable and tCLQV still cannot latch Data out correctly, latch on the next rising edge. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • DQS: Enable DQS. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Enable DTR: Enable DTR. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.

docs.title: Serial PSRAM (Serial Pseudo Static Random Access Memory)
docs.text:
Serial PSRAM is a serial-interface form of PSRAM (Pseudostatic RAM) used to communicate with a microprocessor or other system. PSRAM sits between DRAM and SRAM: it offers DRAM-like density with relatively simple SRAM-like operation and simpler memory control.

docs.title: Serialized IRQ
docs.text:
Serialized IRQ/Data is a communication protocol composed of two lines, PCI-Clock and IRQSER, used to transmit interrupt status. An IRQSER cycle essentially consists of three parts: Start, IRQ/Data, and Stop Frame. The operating modes are Continuous mode and Quiet mode. In Continuous mode, the source of the Start Frame is not restricted; in Quiet mode, only the Host can generate the Start Frame signal.

For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
Serialized IRQ Decode Settings
  • CLOCK: PCI Clock channel.
  • IRQSER: IRQSER channel.
  • Normal: Expand signals of the same frame on one line. Default is this mode selected.
    • Show repeat frame: Show repeated frames. Field enabled (Enable) when checked (Normal mode only). Default is unchecked (hide repeat frames).
  • Advance: Spread all IRQ/Data in a frame across different lines.
  • High Active: Adjust numeric judgment for High Active. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
Normal: hide repeat frames (Default) Normal: show repeat frames Advance: IRQ/Data on separate lines

docs.title: SGPIO (Serial General Purpose Input/Output)
docs.text:
SGPIO (Serial General Purpose Input/Output) is a serial general-purpose I/O interface that you can control for input and output.

Incorrect Mode, latch, or Significant Bit settings can cause decode failure. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
SGPIO Decode Settings
  • Channel: Assign Clock, Load, Data Out (DO), and Data In (DI); enable DO only, DI only, or both (at least one required). Default is DO/DI both checked.
  • Mode: Decode mode.
    • 3-bit Driver: 3-bit driver mode. Default selects this mode.
    • User Defined Data: Custom data mode; Byte/Packet/Latch settings below are field enabled (Enable) only in this mode.
  • Byte per column: Bits per column (8-bits/16-bits). Default is 16-bits.
  • Packets Starts From: Packet starts from High or Low. Default is Low.
  • Load Latch On: Latch on Rising or Falling edge of Load. Default is Rising.
  • SGPMO Latch On: Latch on Rising or Falling edge of SGPMO. Default is Rising.
  • SGPMI Latch On: Latch on Rising or Falling edge of SGPMI. Default is Falling.
  • Display: Show DataOut or DataIn in the waveform area. Field enabled (Enable) when both DO and DI are on. Default is DataOut.
  • Significant Bit: LSB or MSB first. Default is LSB.

docs.title: Smart Card (ISO7816)
docs.text:
Smart Card is a communication protocol based on the ISO 7816 specification, generally used in IC cards or IC chip cards. Different IC chips have different functions and applications. It is mainly used for identification, recording, and encoding/decoding.

Incorrect Baud Rate, initial state, or Reset Timeout relative to the card causes decode failures. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
Smart Card (ISO7816) Decode Settings
  • Channel:
    • CLK: Clock channel. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is checked.
    • DATA: Data pin for transfer (required).
    • RST: Reset channel. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is checked.
  • Baud Rate: Baud rate (including AUTO detection). Default is AUTO.
  • Initial State: Decode start state (Reset / ATR.* / APDU.*). Default is Reset (waiting for ATR).
  • Reset Timeout (ETU): Reset timeout in ETU (T=0 WWT commonly 9600). Default is 9600.
  • MSB first: Use MSB-first bit order. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.
  • Invert: Invert data. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.

docs.title: SMBus (SBS SPD) (System Management Bus)
docs.text:
SMBus (System Management Bus) is a two-wire bus (Clock / Data) derived from I2C, defined by Intel in 1995; typical clock 10 kHz–100 kHz. It can decode SMBus, SBS (Smart Battery), and SPD (Serial Presence Detect).

Wrong address mode or PEC / SBS / SPD options yields wrong report fields. See Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
SMBus Decode Settings
  • Channel:
    • SMBCLK: Clock channel.
    • SMBDATA: Data channel.
  • PEC: Packet Error Code. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
  • 8-bit addressing (Include R/W in Address): Show 8-bit address (with R/W). Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
  • Show SBS: Show Smart Battery System in the report. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
  • Show SPD: Show Serial Presence Detect. Field enabled (Enable) when checked (SPD type list). Default: cleared.
  • Clock Stretching: Detect clock stretching. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared (timeout often 35000).
  • Ignore Glitch: Ignore short glitches. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: checked, < 2 sample points.

docs.text:
SMI (Serial Microprocessor Interface), defined by BDNC, uses one Clock line and one Data line.

Wrong CLK/Data assignment prevents correct decode. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
SMI Decode Settings
  • CLK: Clock channel for data transfer.
  • Data: Data channel for data transfer.

docs.title: SpaceWire
docs.text:
SpaceWire (ECSS-E-ST-50-12C) is the onboard data-handling link used on spacecraft. Each direction carries two lines, Data and Strobe: exactly one of them changes per bit, so the clock is recovered as Data XOR Strobe and no separate clock line is needed. A full-duplex link is therefore four signals.

The standard fixes a 2 Mb/s minimum and a mandatory 10 Mb/s start-up rate, but sets no maximum — the ceiling comes from the equipment and from the skew between the Data and Strobe lines. The decode measures the rate on each direction independently and reports it, so the two directions may run at different rates.

Probe all four signals for a full-duplex measurement, or two for a single direction. If Data and Strobe are swapped on a pair, Auto-detect Data / Strobe resolves it and the report says what it resolved to.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
SpaceWire Decode Settings
  • Full duplex (4 channels): Decode both directions. When cleared, only the Tx pair is read and everything that lives across the two directions — flow-control credit, the initialisation handshake, and which end caused a disconnect — cannot be shown. Default: checked.
  • Auto-detect Data / Strobe: Work out which line of each pair is Data and which is Strobe. Swapping them still yields a valid clock, so the mistake does not stop the decode — it silently corrupts the data. Leave this on unless you have a reason not to. Default: checked.
  • Tx swapped / Rx swapped: State the assignment by hand. Enabled only when Auto-detect is cleared, because auto-detection overwrites them. Default: cleared.
  • Tolerance: How far a bit may deviate from the measured bit period before it is treated as a fault, from 5 % to 50 %. Raise it for a long cable or a link with visible skew. Default: 30 %.
  • Disconnect: How long the line may stop transitioning before the link is reported as disconnected, from 727 ns to 4000 ns. The standard defines a window rather than one value. Default: 850 ns.
  • View: Which layer the waveform and the report present.Field — the parts inside one character: the data bits, the parity bit and the data-control flag. Use it when characters are not decoding at all.Character — one row per character or control code.Packet — one row per packet, with the cargo bytes.Credit — flow-control credit over time; the only view that needs both directions, and therefore the only one not available in Live mode.Default: Character.
  • Waveform: Which direction the waveform strip draws. Outside Live mode the report carries both. At the same bit rate the two directions' characters land almost on top of each other, so drawing both in one row would leave most blocks a single sample wide — this picks one. Enabled only in full duplex. Default: Tx.
  • Packet row: How many cargo bytes one row of the packet report carries before the packet continues on the next row. SpaceWire packets have no maximum length, so long packets always wrap; the continuation rows are marked with the byte offset (008h, 010h, …) and the last row carries the total. Enabled in Packet view. Default: 8 bytes.
  • Reduce repeated NULL / FCT: Collapse a run of NULLs or FCTs into one row. An idle link transmits NULLs continuously, so a real capture is mostly NULLs and the packets are lost among them. Enabled in the views that aggregate rows. Default: checked.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Character view: both directions, with a packet and a Time-code

Each direction has its own Event, Error and Delta columns, so the two streams stay readable side by side. Delta is the interval to the previous event in the same direction.

In Packet view a packet becomes one row, and a payload too long for one row continues on the next:

Packet view: continuation rows and the byte total

docs.title: Live mode
docs.text:
SpaceWire decoding supports Live mode (decoding while a capture is still running), with the limitations below. The decoder follows the stream as it arrives: characters are decoded batch by batch, and character synchronisation - which happens only once, when the link starts - is carried across the batches.

Three things a live decode cannot show. All three are available as usual once the capture has been saved and decoded from the file.

  • The report shows one direction only - the one the waveform strip is set to (the Waveform setting). The waveform strip has always drawn a single direction, and in Live mode the report is built from the same stream. The report states which direction it is showing.
  • Credit view is not available. An FCT travels the opposite way from the data it authorises, so credit can only be worked out with both directions in front of you. Selecting it in Live mode reports the Character view instead and says so in the Information column, rather than showing a credit figure that would drift into a false credit error on a healthy link.
  • The measured bit-rate row is not shown, for the same reason: it travels in the report's own stream rather than in the waveform stream.

docs.title: S/PDIF (Sony/Philips Digital Interconnect Format)
docs.text:
S/PDIF (Sony/Philips Digital Interconnect Format) is a digital audio interface over copper or optical fiber. It is derived from AES/EBU with simplifications for lower-cost hardware.

Wrong Bit Rate/Frame count/parity/data format settings cause decode or playback issues. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
S/PDIF Decode Settings
  • Channel: Assign the S/PDIF signal channel.
  • Auto detect Bit Rate: Automatically detect source bit rate (about 384 kb/s–12.288 Mb/s). Field enabled (Enable) when checked; when cleared, select a built-in bit rate. Default is checked.
  • Num of frame: Frames per block, used to order sub-frames and decode User/Channel status bits. Default is 192.
  • Bit Order (Aux. Data): LSB first or MSB first. Default is LSB first.
  • Bit Order (Audio Data): LSB first or MSB first. Default is LSB first.
  • Data format: 16/20/24 bits. Default is 16.
  • Parity mode: Even/Odd/Non parity. Default is Even parity.
  • Playback: Collect sub-frames and play audio after analysis. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is checked.
  • Display the audio waveform: Draw the audio waveform in the Waveform Window. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is unchecked.

docs.title: SPI NAND
docs.text:
The SPI NAND Flash Memory series uses the SPI/QPI protocol. SPI NAND bus analysis shows command and I/O bus information while viewing signals, reducing time spent on SPI waveform analysis.

Incorrect Vendor, timing, or read mode versus the IC can cause decode errors. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
SPI NAND Decode Settings
  • CS#: Chip Select.
  • SCLK: Clock.
  • SIO0 – SIO3: Data pins (including WP/HOLD#).
  • Vendor/IC: Select vendor and IC; switching may update default timing. Default is Micron (first IC in the list).
  • Start up reading mode: Initial read state (Continuous Read/Buffer Read). Field enabled (Enable) only when the IC supports continuous read. Default is Continuous Read.
  • Command deselect time: Hold time to treat CS# as inactive (tSHSL). Default is 50 ns (may be overwritten by the IC table after selection).
  • Clock LOW to output valid: Positions actual data (tCLQV). Field enabled (Enable) when Latch on rise is cleared. Default is 15 ns (may be overwritten by the IC table).
  • Refer to #Hold Status: Decode using the #Hold pin state. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is cleared.
  • Latch IC output data on SCK rise edge: Latch and decode IC output on the SCK rising edge. Field enabled (Enable) when checked; tCLQV is field disabled (Disable). Default is cleared.
  • Show Calculated Physical Address From Page Address: Show the full physical address computed from the page address. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is checked.
  • Show all repeated Get/Set Feature Data: Show all repeated Get/Set Feature data. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default is cleared.

docs.text:

When Op Code = Get Feature (0F), the report removes repeated values and marks Duration time.

docs.title: SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface)
docs.text:
SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) is a synchronous serial interface, commonly 4-wire (SCK / CS / SDI / SDO), and also available as 3-wire or 2-wire. Data is clocked with SCK.

Mismatch in SPI Type, Bit Order, or Word Size yields misaligned or wrong data. Without CS (Unused Chip Select), set Clock Idle correctly to separate frames. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
SPI Decode Settings
  • SPI Type: Wiring mode. Default: 3 Wire-SPI (with Chip Select).
    • 4 Wire-SPI: Uses SCK, CS, SDI, and SDO. CS: Active High / Active Low; SDI / SDO: Rising / Falling. Display: SDI only / SDO only / Both. Defaults for this type: CS = Active High, SDI = Rising, SDO = Falling, display = Both.
    • 3 Wire-SPI: Uses SCK, CS, and one Data line. Check SDI(Write)-Waiting-SDO(Read) for half-duplex bit counts. Defaults for this type: CS = Active Low, Data = Rising; half-duplex cleared (write / read / wait bits often 8 / 8 / 2).
    • 3 Wire-SPI (Unused Chip Select): Uses SCK, SDI, and SDO without CS. Set Clock Idle to separate frames. Display: SDI only / SDO only / Both. Defaults for this type: SDI / SDO = Rising, display = Both, Idle = 300 ns.
    • 2 Wire-SPI (Unused Chip Select): Uses SCK and SDA without CS. Set Clock Idle. Defaults for this type: Data = Rising, Idle = 300 ns; half-duplex cleared.
  • Clock Channel (SCK): Assign the clock channel.
  • Use External clock: Use an external clock. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
  • Bit Order: LSB First / MSB First. Default: MSB First.
  • Word Size: Bits per data word (4–40). Default: 8.
  • Data valid from SCK: Sample delay from the SCK edge (0–3 sample points). Default: 0 (no delay).
  • Report:
    • Show Idle state in report window: Show Idle in the report. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: checked.
    • Reduce report: Compact the report. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
    • Show data in report (Column): Data columns in the report (1–16). Default: 16.
4 Wire-SPI 3 Wire-SPI (with Chip Select; half-duplex optional) 3 Wire-SPI (Unused Chip Select) 2 Wire-SPI (Unused Chip Select)

Without CS, when Idle ≠ 0, a clock pause longer than Idle separates frames:

Unused Chip Select: frame separation by Clock Idle

Idle = 0 treats the stream as continuous data:

Unused Chip Select: Idle = 0 (continuous data)

docs.title: SSI (Synchronous Serial Interface)
docs.text:
The Synchronous Serial Interface (SSI) protocol has four kinds of signals: Serial Clock (SCK), Transmit Data, Receive Data, and Transmit/Receive Frame Sync (FS). SSI supports Normal or Network mode, independent of whether the transmitter and receiver are synchronous or asynchronous.

Wrong Mode/Line Of Data settings misread frames. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
SSI Decode Settings
  • Channel: Assign SCK/FS/DATA channels on the logic analyzer.
  • Mode: Normal or Network. Default is Normal.
  • Line Of Data: Transmit (Tx) or Receive (Rx). Default is Tx.
  • Merge continuous unknown: Merge consecutive unknown data. Field enabled (Enable) only in Network Receive mode; otherwise Field disabled (Disable). Default is Field disabled (Disable).

docs.title: ST7669
docs.text:
ST7669 was developed by Sitronix for LCD module interfaces.

Incorrect Type changes whether A0/LCD SI are available and can cause decode mismatch. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
ST7669 Decode Settings
  • Type: Interface type. Default is 8-bit Serial Interface.
    • 8-bit Serial Interface (A0 field enabled (Enable); LCD SI field disabled (Disable))
    • 8-bit Serial Interface + LCD SI (A0/LCD SI both field enabled (Enable))
    • 9-bit Serial Interface (A0/LCD SI both field disabled (Disable))
    • 9-bit Serial Interface + LCD SI (A0 field disabled (Disable); LCD SI field enabled (Enable))
  • Chip Select Channel (/CS): CS channel.
  • Clock Channel (SCL): Clock channel.
  • Serial Data Input (MPU SI): MPU serial data input.
  • Serial Data Input (LCD SI): LCD serial data input (enabled by Type).
  • A0: A0 channel (enabled by Type).

docs.title: SWD (Serial Wire Debug)
docs.text:
SWD (Serial Wire Debug) is an ARM test protocol on SWDIO and SWDCLK. It provides access to the CoreSight™ Debug Access Port and can replace JTAG when pin count is limited.

Wrong Bit Order or AP type yields incorrect register interpretation. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
SWD Decode Settings
  • SWDIO: I/O signal channel.
  • SWDCLK: Clock signal channel.
  • Select Reg startup: When the AP Select Register initial value is unknown, the LA shows addresses instead of register names; set Bank and Ctrl/Select manually. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared; Bank/CtrlSel Default: 0/0.
  • Bit Order: LSB or MSB. Default: LSB First.
  • Show DP Reg bit assignments: Show DP register field meanings. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
  • AP Setting: Decode AP registers as MEM-AP, JTAG-AP, or Other. Other shows only Bank X Register X. Default: Other.
AP Setting options
  • Show AP Reg bit assignments: Show AP register field meanings; field enabled (Enable) when MEM-AP or JTAG-AP is selected. Default: cleared.
  • MEM-AP startup: When MEM-AP is selected, initialize MEM-AP contents; matching addresses update during capture. Checking Endian enables (Enable) data with read/write addresses. Default Endian: cleared; Endian type index 0 (Big); TAR Auto-Inc index 0 (Off); Access Size index 0 (8 Bits).
MEM-AP startup
  • Filter Setting: Filter registers you do not need to observe. Default: registers checked (shown).
  • Enable Glitch Filter: Enable glitch filtering. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.

docs.title: SWIM (Single Wire Interface Module)
docs.text:
SWIM is the single-wire debug interface for STM8 8-bit MCUs. While the CPU runs, SWIM allows non-intrusive on-the-fly read/write access to RAM and peripheral registers for debug.

For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

SWIM Decode Settings

SWP (Single Wire Protocol), standardized by ETSI, connects a SIM card and an NFC chip.

S2 requires converting the current-domain signal to voltage before probing; choosing the wrong layer (MAC/LLC) fails decode. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: TDM (Time-Division Multiplexing)
docs.text:
TDM Audio (Time Division Multiplexing Audio) transmits multiple audio channels over a single data line (or a pair) by dividing the stream into time slots. It is common in professional audio, consumer electronics, and automotive digital-audio systems.

Wrong Slot bits/Audio bits/channel count or Mode fails decode. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
TDM Decode Settings
  • Channel:
    • Clock (SCK): Clock channel.
    • Data (SD): Data channel.
    • Word Select (WS): Word Select channel.
  • Audio Settings:
    • Slot bits: Data width of an audio channel. Default: 16.
    • Audio bits: Valid bits in the slot. Default: 16.
    • Channel Count: Number of audio channels. Default: 2.
    • Latch Edge: Latch data on Falling or Rising edge. Default: Falling.
    • Enable Pulse: Active pulse polarity (Low/High). Default: High.
    • Data Offset: Bit offset before data starts. Default: 0.
    • LSB First: Check when data is LSB first. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
    • Save as CSV file: Save decode results as CSV. Field enabled (Enable) when checked. Default: cleared.
    • Mode Select: Data arrangement (Slot Width Mode, Bit Width Mode, I2S Mode, and related options). Default: Slot Width Mode.
  • Sound Reduction: After decode, save, play back, or plot audio (max 8 channels). Field enabled (Enable) when a sub-option is checked. Defaults: cleared.
    • Display the audio waveform: Plot the audio waveform.
    • Enable full scale: Enable full-scale display.
    • Save as WAV file: Save as .WAV.
    • Align common sampling rate: Align to a common sampling rate.
    • Playback: Play All/5 Sec/3 Sec. Default: All (disabled while the group is cleared).

docs.title: UART (RS232) (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter)
docs.text:
UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) is an EIA serial interface. RS-232/RS-485 send characters as a bit stream; RS-485 is differential and must be converted to logic levels before LA measurement.

Wrong Baud Rate or Polarity scrambles decode—prefer Auto Detect. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
UART Decode Settings
  • Channel:
    • Tx: Assign the Tx channel.
    • Rx: Assign the Rx channel. Field enabled (Enable) when selected. Default: cleared.
  • Auto Detect: Auto-detect format options. Field enabled (Enable) when selected. Default: cleared.
  • Baud Rate: Bits per second. Wrong rate fails decode. Default: 9600.
  • Polarity: Idle High / Idle Low. Wrong polarity reverses Start/Stop. Default: Idle High.
  • Parity: None / Odd / Even / Mark / Space. Default: None.
  • Data Bits: 4–16. Default: 8.
  • Stop Bits: 1–4.5. Default: 1.
  • MSB First: MSB after Start when selected; otherwise LSB. Default: cleared.
  • Invert Bits: Invert High/Low. Field enabled (Enable) when selected. Default: cleared.
  • Show S/P: Show Start/Stop in the waveform. Field enabled (Enable) when selected. Default: cleared.
  • Show ASCII: Show ASCII in the report. Field enabled (Enable) when selected. Default: cleared.
  • Waveform Area Settings:
    • Decode: Show Rx or Tx in the waveform. Rx only when Rx is field enabled (Enable). Default: Tx.
    • Show Scale: Show the scale. Field enabled (Enable) when selected. Default: cleared.
  • Report Area Settings:
    • Idle, Break Line Wrap: Wrap on Idle/Break. Field enabled (Enable) when selected. Default: cleared.
    • Show Idle State: Show Idle state. Default: cleared.
    • Report Size: Data fields (16 / 32). Default: 16.
    • Line Wrap (<= 8Bits): Wrap by data pattern (1st/2nd). Default: cleared (pattern often 0A).

docs.title: UFCS (Universal Fast Charging Specification)
docs.text:
UFCS (Universal Fast Charging Specification) defines a unified fast-charging standard for mobile terminals to improve interoperability. The supply port uses USB Type-A; signaling follows USB D+/D-.

For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

UFCS Decode Settings

docs.title: ULPI (UTMI+ Low Pin Interface)
docs.text:
ULPI (UTMI+ Low Pin Interface) is the low-pin version of UTMI. UTMI (USB 2.0 Transceiver Macrocell Interface) connects a USB controller and USB PHY; compared with ULPI, UTMI has more control signals and supports 8-bit/16-bit data interfaces.

Choosing the wrong Decode mode (ULPI/USB) misinterprets traffic. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.text:
ULPI Decode Settings
  • Channel: Assign ULPI channels; Quick Setting can set Data pins quickly. Quick Setting Default is checked (enabled).

docs.title: UNI/O
docs.text:
UNI/O is a Microchip single-wire bus protocol mainly used with EEPROM. It targets fewer I/O pins in compact embedded systems and uses Manchester Encoding at about 10 kbps–100 kbps.

Wrong address width or tolerance settings cause decode failures. For channel-prefix differences, see Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
UNI/O Decode Settings
  • Channel: Assign the SCIO channel on the logic analyzer.
  • Device Address: Device address width (8 Bits / 12 Bits). Default is 8 Bits.
  • Tolerance: Input / Output edge jitter tolerance. Default is Input 10% and Output 25%.
  • Report Setting: Data columns in the report (8 / 16). Default is 8 columns.

docs.title: USB PD 3 (USB Power Delivery)
docs.text:
USB PD (Power Delivery) 2.0/3.0 uses BMC (Biphase Mark Coding) for Type-C power/charging (laptops, tablets, phones, power banks, etc.); up to 240 W (e.g. Rev 3.1).

Wrong CC wiring or VDM config affects decode and vendor messages. See Settings.

docs.title: Decode Settings
docs.text:
USB PD Decode Settings
  • Channel: Configuration Channel (CC) **CC1** and **CC2**.
  • VDM: When checked, field enabled (Enable) Vendor Defined Message; reads Structured VDM SVID/Command from the config file (Edit/Refresh).
VDM configure file format
  • Up to 32 VDMs (##VDM1–##VDM32). Leading ##XXX is a keyword—do not reuse elsewhere. Each VDM has a Header (first Data Object) plus VDO(s) for the Command response.
  • Header is wrapped by two #Header lines for SVID/Command. Example: Bits<31:16>,8087,Intel Vendor-defined message; Bits<4:0>,10,DISCOVER_BUTTONS.
  • VDOs use #VDO 1, #VDO 2, … for bit fields (reserved or function bits). Other Commands (e.g. 1Ch) can be separate ##VDM blocks.
  • Show 5b value in waveform: Show 5b instead of 4b when checked. Default: cleared.

docs.title: USB4/TBT3 SB Channel
docs.text:
USB4 can carry DisplayPort video and PCIe through Intel tunneling and supports PD (Power Delivery). It is backward compatible with USB 2.0 and USB 3.2 Gen1/Gen2 and supports Thunderbolt 3/4. In USB 3.2 the sideband (SB) channel carried Alt-Mode video-protocol traffic (for example DP Alt-Mode AUX over sideband). docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
MII (Media Independent Interface), RMII (Reduced MII), RGMII (Reduced Gigabit MII), and GMII (Gigabit MII) are a family of standard interfaces used to connect Ethernet MAC (Media Access Control) controllers to PHY (Physical Layer) transceivers. Originally defined in IEEE 802.3, these interfaces provide a standardized way to separate the MAC logic (typically integrated in SoCs, microcontrollers, or FPGAs) from the PHY chip that handles the actual electrical signaling on the Ethernet cable. This separation allows flexible hardware design where different PHYs can be paired with various MAC implementations without custom integration.

Each variant represents a different trade-off between pin count, clock frequency, implementation complexity, and cost. The evolution of these interfaces reflects the increasing demands of Ethernet speeds and the ongoing need to reduce system cost and complexity:

  • MII - The original 10/100 Mbps interface (1995)
  • RMII - Reduced pin count version of MII
  • GMII - Gigabit extension of MII
  • RGMII - Reduced pin count Gigabit interface

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Standardized Interface: IEEE-defined specifications ensure broad compatibility
  • MAC-PHY Separation: Clean architectural boundary for flexible design
  • Multiple Speed Support: Auto-negotiation and speed adaptation (10/100/1000 Mbps)
  • Bidirectional Communication: Separate TX and RX datapaths
  • Management Interface: MDC/MDIO sideband for PHY configuration (IEEE 802.3 Clause 22/45)
  • Pin Count Options: From 7 pins (RMII) to 24 pins (GMII) depending on variant
  • Clock Flexibility: Various clocking modes (source from MAC or PHY)
  • Error Signaling: Dedicated signals for RX/TX errors
  • Industry Standard: Supported by all major Ethernet PHY and MAC vendors

docs.title: Variant Comparison
docs.text: Interface Data Width Clock Freq Pin Count Speed Year MII 4-bit 2.5/25 MHz 16 10/100 Mbps 1995 RMII 2-bit 50 MHz 7 10/100 Mbps 1998 GMII 8-bit 2.5/25/125 MHz 24 10/100/1000 Mbps 1998 RGMII 4-bit DDR 125 MHz 12 10/100/1000 Mbps 2000

docs.title: Common Applications
docs.text:
Embedded Systems - Microcontroller-based Ethernet devices (RMII common) - IoT gateways and edge computing devices - Industrial control and automation systems - Single-board computers (Raspberry Pi, BeagleBone)

Network Infrastructure - Ethernet switches and routers - Network interface cards (NICs) - Media converters - PoE (Power over Ethernet) devices

Consumer Electronics - Smart TVs and set-top boxes - Gaming consoles - Home automation hubs - Network-attached storage (NAS)

Automotive - In-vehicle infotainment systems - ADAS (Advanced Driver Assistance Systems) - Automotive Ethernet gateways - Telematics control units

Industrial/Commercial - Factory automation equipment - Building management systems - Security and surveillance systems - Point-of-sale terminals

Test and Measurement - Network analyzers - Traffic generators - Protocol analyzers - Embedded test equipment

docs.title: Choosing an Interface
docs.text:
Use MII when: - Need 10/100 Mbps with simple design - PCB space and pins are not critical - Legacy compatibility required - Separate TX/RX clocks beneficial

Use RMII when: - Pin count is constrained - 10/100 Mbps sufficient - Embedded microcontroller application - Shared clock simplifies design

Use GMII when: - Need Gigabit Ethernet - Pin count not constrained - Simple SDR design preferred - Internal FPGA/ASIC implementation

Use RGMII when: - Need Gigabit with minimal pins - PCB routing complexity acceptable - DDR-capable MAC and PHY available - Most common Gigabit interface choice
